title: Visit non-adjacent houses
statement:
A fundraiser walks down a street of houses in a row; `gifts[i]` is what house i would donate. Neighbors talk to each other, so if you visit a house you cannot also visit the house right next to it.

Return the most you can collect.

examples.explanation: Visit houses 0 and 3 for 6 + 9 = 15, or houses 0, 2 and 4 for 11.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Is the street a straight line, not a circle?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: A straight line; the first and last houses are not neighbors.
clarifyingQuestions.why: The circular version needs two passes.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can gifts be zero?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes, gifts are zero or more.
clarifyingQuestions.why: Skipping is never worse than taking a zero.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What if there are no houses?

edgeCases.why: The best plan skips two houses in a row.
Take the larger of two neighbors.

approaches.name: Try every valid subset
approaches.idea: Recursively decide visit or skip for each house.

optimal.name: Two running values
optimal.explanation: Track take = best total if you visit the current house and skip = best total if you do not. For each gift g: new take = skip + g, new skip = max(take, skip). Return max(take, skip).

hintLadder: Does always taking every other house work? Try [5, 1, 1, 5].
At each house you either visit it or not. What does each choice depend on?
Define the best total up to house i.
best(i) = max(best(i - 1), best(i - 2) + gifts[i]), keeping only two values.

expectedMentions.what: Asks whether the street wraps around
Explains why taking every other house fails
Reduces to O(1) space with two variables

walkthrough.say: The street is a line, so the first and last aren’t neighbors? Gifts are never negative, and no houses means zero?
Taking every other house doesn’t work: for 5, 1, 1, 5 the best is the two 5s, skipping two in the middle.

At each house I either visit it, which means I skipped the previous one, or I skip it and keep the best so far. So I track two numbers: the best if I take this house and the best if I don’t. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space.
Taking this house adds to the old skip. Skipping keeps the better of the two.
For 6, 1, 2, 9, 3: after 6, take 6, skip 0. After 1, take 1, skip 6. After 2, take 8, skip 6. After 9, take 15, skip 8. After 3, take 11, skip 15. Answer 15.
For 5, 1, 1, 5: after the third house, skip is 5 and take is 6. Taking the last 5 adds to skip, giving 10, while skip becomes 6. Answer 10, the two 5s, which skips two houses in a row.
O(n) time, O(1) space. For a circular street, run it twice: once without the first house and once without the last.
